Organizational Leadership BAAS completion family

Investigate this applied completion family when professional or occupational learning fits your background. Separate the Texas core, professional-development electives and applied major.

What makes this route worth exploring

  • Applied prior-learning evaluation
  • Competency-based delivery where offered
  • Core/major/elective separation
  • Residence-specific cost comparison

What needs to be confirmed

  • Verify the active degree under the current university name/catalog.
  • Texas-specific core requirements need accepted matches.
  • Historical sources conflict about an upper-level institutional subset.
  • Residence and eligibility change the applicable tuition quote.

Eligibility and your situation

  • Ask whether technical, occupational and military learning meets entry and placement rules.
  • Confirm current program availability and residence-based charges.

A practical sequence

  1. Confirm current award, admission gates and catalog.
  2. Evaluate academic, technical, military and professional records.
  3. Map Texas core, professional-development and applied-major blocks.
  4. Resolve institutional/upper-level requirements with the university.
  5. Complete approved gaps and required major assessments.
  6. Reconcile final audit, charges and graduation.

Your next useful actions

  • Request the current BAAS audit.
  • Ask for written institutional/upper-level rules and Texas-core placement.
  • Obtain a residence-specific complete-price quote.
